title: Permit Hot Potato
oneLiner: 한 명이 건설안을 내면 나머지는 비밀 이해관계자로 20초씩 양보를 요구하고, 계획을 망치지 않은 채 네 표를 모아야 하는 협상 파티게임.
theme: 역전 — a tiny stakeholder card can overturn the mayor's grand plan.
targetUser: friends, classrooms, streamers, planners, and urban-policy communities.
keyUX: deal proposal → secret role reveal → timed demand → drag one concession onto the plan → simultaneous stamps → side-effect burst → clip/rematch.

sourceSignals.note: Permit Pending makes concessions, public hearings, and votes playable.

mechanic: one proposal, four secret interests, one concession per player, simultaneous vote, visible project deformation.
triggerMoment: the mayor reveals a seemingly perfect project and the first objection clock starts.
buyerShareAudience: party-game players, educators, event hosts, and viewers.
userActionSentence: “네 표를 얻되, 원래 짓고 싶던 건 남겨야 해요.”
threeSecondSting: a beautiful park sits under four locked vote stamps and the line “20초마다 하나를 양보하세요.”
outputArtifact: deformed before/after proposal poster, vote breakdown, and seven-second failure clip.
firstValidationTest: run 30 four-player rounds; measure rule comprehension under 15 seconds, negotiation completion, laughter/fail clips, and rematch rate.
lovedBySmallGroup: 4/5 — urbanism nerds, civics classes, tabletop groups, and streamers enjoy arguing over tradeoffs.
smallGroupFit: four people can play from a link without learning a city simulation.
spreadTrigger: every failed vote produces a 7-second “concession pile” clip showing who killed the project and why.
referencePattern: city hearing + Hot Potato timer + simultaneous party-game vote.
twist: concessions physically mutate the shared plan, so “winning” with an unrecognizable project is a comic failure.
firstScreen: one attractive proposal, four sealed stakeholder cards, four vote stamps, and a 20-second rule.
shareOrPlayLoop: propose → object → concede → stamp → explode side effects → clip → swap mayor → rematch.
dopamineHook: thumping objection timer, magnetic concession snap, last-second stamp flip, absurd side-effect pop, seven-second recap, rematch under ten seconds.
planBrief: Opportunity: policy conflict is inherently dramatic when consequences are visible. Inflow: party link, stream, or classroom. Validation: comprehension/rematch/clips. Core loop: proposal → roles → demands → concessions → vote → result. First screen teaches the whole rule. Rules: one demand and one concession each; no real political persuasion data. QA: late join, tie, all-no, over-conceded plan, color blindness, reduced motion, classroom-safe names. Risk: complexity; keep each card to one sentence.
developmentStartPrompt: Build a four-player browser party-game simulation with proposal, secret interests, 20-second demand turns, drag-and-snap concessions, simultaneous vote stamps, visible plan deformation, side-effect burst, seven-second recap, mayor swap, and instant rematch.
stitchPrompt: Create a responsive four-player party game called “Permit Hot Potato.” The entire rule must fit in one sentence on the first screen: “Win four votes, but do not concede away the thing you wanted to build.” Open on a beautiful riverside park proposal surrounded by four locked vote stamps and four sealed stakeholder cards. The mayor reveals the plan; each player sees one secret interest, gets 20 seconds to demand one concession, and the mayor drags exactly one change onto the shared plan. After four rounds, all stamps flip together. Make concessions visibly deform the project—parking swallows the trees, height limits crush housing, noise walls block the river—so winning an absurd plan is also funny. Include tie, all-no, over-conceded, surprise-support, classroom-safe, reduced-motion, seven-second recap, mayor swap, and rematch states. Required sections: room, proposal, secret cards, timer, concession tray, vote stamps, side effects, result poster, clip, and rematch. Design direction: use the playful-experimental profile with deep plum, one hot coral accent, oversized stamps, chunky 12px cards, elastic snap motion, stable central geometry, and no city-management dashboard or copied SimCity branding.
